The Laxey Wheel, built in 1854, is a large waterwheel built above the village of Laxey in the Isle of Man which has a 72-foot-6-inch (22.1 m) diameter, is 6 feet (1.83 m) wide and revolves at approximately three revolutions per minute.

The wheel was used to pump water from the Glen Mooar part of the ‘Great Laxey Mines’ industrial complex. A water-powered wheel was used since the Isle of Man does not have a supply of coal for a steam-powered pump. It is still the largest working waterwheel in the world. It is featured on the reverse side of the £20 notes issued by the Isle of Man.
